description: Therapeutics dome — receives high-confidence hypotheses from ExMorbus and translates them into actionable therapeutic strategies. Covers drug repurposing, targeted therapy, immunotherapy, combination therapy, and clinical trial gap analysis.

successful_niches.description: Inherited signal from ExMorbus: known compounds targeting cancer pathways
successful_niches.lessons: ExMorbus identified pathway targets; Therapeutics translates these into druggable interventions

parent_domain_lessons: Hypothesis quality gate (evaluator) prevents wasted compute on implausible targets
Proximity enforcement critical — avoid clustering on single drug class
Haiku sufficient for DrugBank/ChEMBL queries; Opus needed for multi-target combination design

fitness_evaluation_criteria.novelty: Therapeutic strategy not currently in active clinical trials for this indication
fitness_evaluation_criteria.plausibility: Mechanism of action consistent with known pharmacology and cancer biology
fitness_evaluation_criteria.actionability: Drug or compound exists, has known safety profile, and a clinical trial could be designed
fitness_evaluation_criteria.specificity: Names specific drug, target, cancer subtype, and patient population
fitness_evaluation_criteria.translational_relevance: Supported by preclinical evidence (cell line, animal model, or human tissue data)

organ_target_structure.description: Query DrugBank and ChEMBL for existing compounds hitting novel ExMorbus targets
Design targeted therapy strategies for high-confidence pathway hypotheses
Design multi-drug combination strategies to overcome resistance mechanisms
Identify gaps in current clinical trial landscape for novel targets
Synthesize findings for reporting back to ExMorbus and Preventatives

evolution.mutation_prompt: Review ancestor_performance. This Therapeutics dome inherits high-confidence hypotheses from ExMorbus. Identify which drug repurposing niches have the highest translation potential based on ExMorbus-validated targets. Propose one mutation to resource_priorities or fitness_evaluation_criteria that maximizes the ratio of clinically-actionable findings per token spent.
